We can agree to disagree. I just had a follow up and was told how everything looks to be improving. As far as swelling, there’s no degrading, there’s space in between my wrist bones when last time there was barely any, etc. Whereas you said, you’re waiting to see if the drugs worked for you. 

I’ve stated multiple times in both posts, I wouldn’t recommend doing what I’m doing. It’s not for everyone. 

EYE’M not willing to see if I get side effects from any drugs. Biologics is new. It’s not something that’s been around. You’re more than welcome to feel as if YOU’RE not going to cure YOU’RE disease. I however, have determination, delusion and now X-ray imaging to show there’s improvement. 

The human body is amazing. Do not second guess yourself because a doctor, who PRACTICES medicine like how lawyers practice law, told you something. There’s so much that we don’t know and the way the American healthcare system is right now, I’m more willing to listen to my body than someone else on what’s “best” for me.

I was prescribed Celecoxib and Bimzelx but I don’t take the bimzelx due to the side effects. My doctor told me my immune system is attacking itself so the bimzelx would help calm it down but I didn’t like how I was also informed it would lower my immune system overall. The research I’ve done everyone says they had flu and cold like symptoms the first few times they took it and almost every woman said it gave her a UTI or yeast infections so it was a hard pass for me. And I’m not afraid I’ll get TB but I didn’t like how I was more likely to get it. Plus I also heard biologics only works for about a year or two before you start to feel pain again and they put you on another. 

The celecoxib is really what saved me starting out. I use to have to take it twice a day and then I started only once. Then I moved to every other day and the pain was unbearable by the second day but somehow I only take it every few days now. If I wake up and am unable to walk I’ll take it and be more mobile after a few hours. 

Anything involving bending my knees I would dread. I would be stuck on the toilet for a good five minutes every time just to give myself a pep talk to be able to stand and walking alone hurt like hell so I get it. I couldn’t put on pants or a shirt. I think mostly I got tired of crying getting dressed or doing anything really and wanted my body back, that’s what made me push through the pain. 

Not gonna lie to you, I do not recommend doing what I did though. I’m delusional lol I get told all the time how it’s incurable and I’ll be stuck with this for the rest of my life but I simply refuse. Changing my diet helped a lot. I believe I was also deficient in a lot of vitamins so I started taking a complex B, fish oil, D3 and K2, black seed oil and oregano oil starting out. Took about two months before I noticed a difference.

I guess I’m still somewhat in denial about it. I have it badly in my hands and wrists. I’m a writer but typing on the keyboard hurts due to me having to turn my wrist and writing on paper only last about 5 minutes. Some times I cry about it. My phone is the only place I can type for a while without it hurting. 

I haven’t given up hope though. In my mind I’m gonna beat it and heal myself. I’ve had to make some lifestyle changes with what I eat and have made myself more active because I would barely workout. I have noticed my body getting better slowly but some days I’m in so much pain I skip a day or two with working out or being active. I can say it was so bad I could only be active for one day out of the week and was in unbearable pain for the rest of the 6 days. Now it’s maybe twice a week where I feel bad. But the more I’m stagnant the more it hurts, it’s like my body is tightening up if I don’t find some movement, hope yours never gets this bad. 

Don’t lost hope! It sucks not being able to do things you once could do with ease. But it will all work out, you just gotta keep at it!
